Malicious Supply-Chain Indicators

No confirmed malicious supply-chain indicators.

Automatic Execution Paths

  • In the provided extracted text, there is no evidence of .pth, sitecustomize.py, usercustomize.py, install-time hooks, or malicious import-time execution.
  • testql/cli.py contains logic in main() to check the PyPI version and, after user confirmation, run pip install --upgrade testql. This path requires the user to invoke the CLI, targets the official PyPI API and the same package, and is not treated as malicious automatic execution evidence.
  • Normal console_scripts/CLI behavior was excluded as automatic execution evidence.

Theft / Exfiltration / Persistence / Lateral Movement / Stealth

  • Credential harvesting: No evidence in the provided files of broad discovery or collection of environment variables, .env files, SSH keys, cloud/CI tokens, wallets, or kubeconfig.
  • Exfiltration/staging: No evidence of uploads to attacker-controlled domains, webhooks, raw IPs, paste/drop services, or archive/base64 staging of harvested files.
  • Persistence: No evidence of cron, systemd, launch agents, shell profile edits, background polling, or self-reinstall persistence loops.
  • Lateral movement: No evidence of Kubernetes service-account abuse, Docker socket access, cloud metadata access, or GitHub Actions/package-registry token abuse.
  • Obfuscation/loaders: The many pre-scan re.compile hits appear to be parser/grammar regular expressions. No evidence of base64/zlib/marshal/eval/exec staged loaders was identified.
  • Network and process-execution hits appear tied to test/CLI/runner functionality, with insufficient evidence connecting them to malicious supply-chain behavior.

Distribution Integrity Anomalies

  • Based on the provided file text, there is no evidence of hidden payloads, unexplained native binaries, typosquatting, sudden dependency insertion, or wheel/sdist mismatch.
  • External links in testql.egg-info/PKG-INFO, README.md, and related metadata appear to be badges/documentation links and are not evidence of malicious distribution integrity anomalies.

Additional Verification Needed

  • The input is limited to 21 selected files out of 302 plus pre-scan results. If present, full setup.py, pyproject.toml, setup.cfg, MANIFEST.in, all package files, binaries/large files, and wheel artifacts should be reviewed.
